chapter_theme: The cosmic linga: the linga is the directions, the arts and the world itself, arising as Shakti and as Sadasiva, who gives enjoyment and release. The gods praise him without understanding; the temple, and many materials matched to each varna, can serve as the linga; and the Lord beyond all knowing makes the body his temple and the cosmos his place of worship.
structure_note: The linga as world, Shakti and Sadasiva (1712 to 1714, linked by repeated words); the gods' praise and the Supreme in all gods (1715, 1716); grace through the fixed form (1717); the temple, the materials and the varnas' lingas (1718 to 1721); the Lord in the body (1722, 1723); the cosmos as his body and as a linga being worshipped (1724, 1725).

1712.reading: No one knows what the linga is: the linga is the eight directions, the linga is the sixty-four arts, and it is the world that has taken form as the linga.
1712.nuance: எண்ணெண் கலை (eight eights) are traditionally the sixty-four arts, though கலை may also mean the kalas of cosmology. The last line can be read either way round: the world rose as the linga, or the linga took up the world.

1713.reading: What arises in the world arises first as Shakti, in Shakti's form and with Shakti's qualities, and what so arises in the world is Sadasiva himself.
1713.nuance: The verse picks up 1712's last word (உலகே) and repeats உலகில் எடுத்தது in every line. In Siddhanta, Sadasiva is the form of Siva where formed and formless meet, the one the linga signifies; the verse makes the world's arising Shakti's and Sadasiva's at once.

1714.reading: Sadasiva remains giving enjoyment, release, understanding and powers, and the oneness beyond the body and the thirty-six tattvas; the six paths of the Agamas too are Siva.
1714.nuance: ஆகமும் may be the body (ஆகம்) or the Agama, which changes what lies beyond the tattvas. ஆகம அத்துவா ஆறும் are the six paths (adhvas) of Agamic cosmology, here declared to be Siva himself.

1715.reading: Countless gods praised our Lord and hailed him as the fragrant fresh south breeze and the bountiful one, yet for all their clamour they do not grasp that he stands beyond the worlds and guards them.
1715.nuance: The south breeze (தென்றல்) is the gentle wind of Tamil poetry. The point is the gap between praise and understanding: the gods worship loudly (ஆர்த்தினர்) but miss what he is.

1716.reading: The bright fire, Brahma, Vishnu, Prajapati, the shining sun and Indra, the gods who mingle everywhere as the light of the eye, are all, as a cool light everywhere, the Supreme.
1716.nuance: ஒண்சுடரோன் may be Agni or Rudra. The play on சுடர் (flame) runs through every line, ending in தண்சுடர் (cool flame). The verse can mean the gods are the Supreme, or that the Supreme pervades them as their light.

1717.reading: Siva can give grace from within the fixed form, yet none worship the truth of the great Supreme; and for those who do, it becomes the golden creeper standing within the flower.
1717.nuance: தாபரம் (the fixed) is traditionally the installed linga, and மாபரம் the Supreme beyond form. பொற்கொடி (golden creeper) is a name for Shakti, and பூவகம் may be the heart lotus. One reading: grace comes through the installed form though few seek the formless, and those who do find Shakti within.

1718.reading: To those who study Hara's state, the raised temple tower is the gross linga, Sadasiva is the fine subtle one, and the altar of offerings is the bhadra linga.
1718.nuance: The verse reads the temple itself as linga in grades: the vimana (தூலம், gross), Sadasiva (சூக்குமம், subtle), and the bali-pitha (பத்திர லிங்கம்), whose name is technical. Its point is that the whole temple is Siva's form.

1719.reading: Pearl, ruby and coral, sacred ash and other substances, cooked and raw rice, flowers and sand: for one who seeks to be saved, any of these can be made the linga, the Father's body.
1719.nuance: The verse lists materials for lingas, many of them temporary ones made for a single worship in Agamic practice. கொத்தும்அக்கொம்பு and கோமளம் are obscure; அத்தன்தன் ஆகமம் may be the Father's body or his Agama. The list says the material matters less than the worship.

1720.reading: Thick curd, ghee, milk, pure wax, refined copper, fire, mercury, water, strong brick, bilva and gold: any one of these, clearly known, can be the Sivalinga.
1720.nuance: A second list of materials. தென்தியங்கு ஒன்றை is unclear; I take ஒன்றை as 'any one'. இரதம் is usually taken as mercury, used for lingas in later Saiva practice.

1721.reading: For Brahmins' worship the linga is of crystal, for kings' worship of gold, for prosperous Vaishyas of komalam, and for Shudras the ancient bana linga.
1721.nuance: The verse assigns materials by varna; it doesn't say one worship is worth more than another. கோமளம் recurs from 1719 and is unclear (perhaps a gem). The bana linga is traditionally a naturally formed stone from a river.

1722.reading: The Lord stood where nothing could know him, even for one who knew and sought his single nature; and he who is the eight worlds of new awareness has, as I have come to know, made my body his temple.
1722.nuance: The demonstratives அது, எது, இது in the first and last lines carry the argument and are hard to fix. புவனங்கள் எட்டும் may be the eight worlds or the eightfold form of Siva. Sengalvaraya compares the last line with Tiruvachakam's Pidiththa Paththu 10, where the Lord enters the body as a golden temple.

1723.reading: Inside the flesh, a place made to fall away, he who is the wide world settles unknown; before the light came, the destroyer of sin, the holy one, stood there as refuge.
1723.nuance: The verse rhymes அகலிடம் (wide place), உகலிடம் (place of falling away), பகலிடம் (place of day) and புகலிடம் (refuge). பகலிடம் ஆம் முனம் may mean before the light of knowledge dawns, or before the day ends.

1724.reading: The earth is his flower-decked feet, the sky his crown that bears the woman, and the Lord's body stands as space: that is how he stands as the origin.
1724.nuance: சூழல் in line 1 is read as கழல் (anklet, feet), which fits the head-to-foot pairing with முடி (crown). The woman on the crown is traditionally Ganga. நீதியுள் may mean 'in right order' or 'the Lord of justice'.

1725.reading: The earth is Shakti as the base and the sky the linga; the wave-beaten sea is its bathing hall, the cloud water on the hills and the stars of the sky its garland, and the directions are the garment of boundless Nandi.
1725.nuance: The cosmos is pictured as a linga in worship: Shakti as the pedestal, the sea for its bath, stars for its garland. கலை is read as garment, the directions clothing Siva, as his name திகம்பரன் says; it can also mean digit or kala.

links.note: 1712 says the world has taken form as the linga; 1725 shows it in worship, with the earth as Shakti's base, the sky as the linga, the sea as its bath and the stars as its garland.

Both say the Lord took up the body as his temple (கோயில் கொண்டான்). In 725 that discovery turns Tirumular from scorning the body to caring for it; in 1722 it follows from the Lord being beyond all knowing.

2104 declares one kulam and one God; 1721 still gives each varna its own linga. The oneness of 2104 does not, in this chapter, remove ritual distinctions by birth, though 1721 claims no difference in worth.

source_issues: 1719: line 4 reads உய்த்த்தின், a misprint, perhaps for உய்த்ததின் or உய்த்தவர்; line 2 (கொத்தும்அக்கொம்பு சிலைநீறு கோமளம்) is obscure.
1720: line 4 (தென்தியங்கு ஒன்றை) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1724: சூழல் in line 1 is probably a misreading of கழல்.
